title: Little Krishna and the pot of butter.
lines: Long ago, in a little village in India called Gokul, lived a little boy.
His name was Krishna.
Krishna was a very special little boy.
His skin was blue, as blue as the sky.
He had big shining eyes, and in his hair he always wore a beautiful peacock feather.
And Krishna was very naughty!
Lots of cows lived in the village.
Every morning the people milked the cows.
From the milk they made butter.
White, soft, creamy butter.
And do you know what Krishna loved to eat most of all?
Butter!
He could never get enough of it.
Mummy Yashoda knew that.
So she put the butter in a big clay pot.
And she hung that pot very high from the ceiling, on a rope.
There, said Mummy.
That little butter thief can't reach it now!
But Krishna was clever.
When Mummy went to the market, he called all his friends.
Come on, let's make a tower!
The biggest boy stood at the bottom.
Another boy climbed onto his shoulders.
And Krishna climbed right to the top.
Wobble, wobble!
Careful!
Krishna stretched out his arms, and yes, he could touch the pot.
He put his hand in and pulled out a big handful of butter.
Mmm!
He gave a little to each friend.
And through the open window a few little monkeys were peeking in.
Ooh ooh, aah aah!
Krishna laughed and threw a blob of butter to the monkeys too.
Here, this is for you!
The monkeys gobbled it up.
But then they heard footsteps.
Oh no!
Mummy Yashoda was coming home!
All the friends jumped down.
Plop, plop, plop!
The monkeys ran off through the window.
And Krishna stood there, in the middle of the kitchen.
Krishna, said Mummy sternly, have you been eating butter?
Me?
said Krishna with big innocent eyes.
No, Mummy, not me!
But Mummy looked at his face.
There was white butter all around his mouth.
On his cheeks.
On his nose.
And even on his peacock feather!
Mummy tried to look cross, but she couldn't.
She had to laugh.
What a naughty little butter thief you are, she said, and she gave him a big hug.
In the afternoon Krishna took the cows to the meadow.
He had a flute with him, a flute made of bamboo.
He sat down under a tree by the river, and he began to play.
What beautiful music!
So soft and so sweet.
And do you know what happened?
All the cows came to him.
They stopped eating grass and came to stand close to Krishna to listen.
Moo, went the cows softly.
The birds stopped singing and listened too.
The peacocks came closer and spread their beautiful feathers.
And even the fish in the river poked their heads above the water.
Krishna's music made everyone calm and happy.
When the sun went down, Krishna walked back home, with all the cows following him, still playing his flute.
Mummy Yashoda was waiting at the door.
Come in, my little blue boy, she said.
I have something tasty for you.
And what do you think it was?
A little bowl of fresh butter!
But this time, just on the table.
